data.title: Branchenregister Musterland – Invoice for registry listing (€569.06)
data.summary: Branchenregister Musterland – Verzeichnisservice sent an "Eintragungsbestätigung und Rechnung" demanding €569.06 for a 24-month "Grundeintrag mit Logo" directory listing, payable by 16 September 2027, in a style typical of the well-known German "Branchenregister" directory-entry scam.
data.explanation: This letter is styled as a confirmation of a registry entry you supposedly requested, but it is really an unsolicited invoice for a paid listing — a pattern long documented as the "Branchenregister"/Adressbuchschwindel scam. Warning signs include a payee name that differs from the sender, a short payment deadline, a threat to go straight to debt collection, and the statement that paying alone creates a contract. There is usually no existing obligation unless you knowingly signed up for this paid service. Do not pay or reply with personal/payment data before checking with a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale); keep the letter in case a collection agency follows up.

warnings: This letter matches the known German "Branchenregister"/Adressbuchschwindel scam pattern: an unsolicited paid directory listing disguised as a confirmation.
The payment recipient named for the transfer, "BRM Verlagsservice Ltd.", differs from the sender named on the letter, "Branchenregister Musterland".
The provided IBAN does not pass standard IBAN checksum validation.
The letter claims that paying the invoice alone creates a binding contract, which pressures payment without a signed agreement.
It threatens to pass the matter to a debt collection agency without any further reminder if not paid by the short deadline, a common pressure tactic.
